title: Cristaux (1970). Gribouillis et calculs divers : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): S is a base scheme and M is a twisted-constant abelian group of finite type over S. G = D(M) is the corresponding group of multiplicative type. ℓ^G_· denotes its co-Lie complex, i.e. e^*L_{G/S}, in the sense used by Mazur–Roberts and Illusie.

Previous page. Grothendieck takes the canonical two-step flat resolution 0→R→Z[M]→M→0 and dualises it to get a resolution of G by tori, 0→G→T→T'→0. The Mazur–Roberts transitivity triangle then gives
ℓ^G ≃ [ω_{T'}→ω_T] ≃ M ⊗^L_Z O_S (1.3).
If O_S is a Λ-algebra, this becomes
ℓ^G ≃ (M⊗^L_Z Λ) ⊗^L_Λ O_S (1.4).

This page.
- (1.4'): if Λ is a field, e.g. F_p (S of characteristic p), then O_S is flat over Λ and the outer derived tensor is unnecessary: ℓ^G ≃ (M⊗^L_Z F_p) ⊗_{F_p} O_S. In other words, the co-Lie complex is the base change to O_S of a two-term complex of F_p-vector spaces with cohomology M/pM in degree 0 and _pM in degree −1.
- 1.5: suppose M is isotrivial, i.e. it is trivialised on a principal covering S'→S with discrete or profinite group π. Then M comes by descent from a (continuous) π-module M_0. Grothendieck's example: fibres of finite type, S normal and connected, S' the (pro-)universal covering, π = π_1.
- (1.6): this situation is encoded as a morphism of topoi f: S (étale, fppf or fpqc topos) → B_π, the classifying topos of π.
- (1.7): M = f^*(M_0).
- Ringing both topoi by the constant ring Λ, f^* is exact and compatible with tensor products. Hence M⊗^L_Z Λ = f^*(M_0⊗^L_Z Λ), and
(1.8) ℓ^G ≃ f^*(M_0⊗^L_Z Λ) ⊗^L_Λ O_S, with the L superfluous when Λ is a field.

Purpose, made explicit on the next page: the canonical invariants of ℓ^G are its cohomology sheaves ω_G = M⊗O_S and n_G = Tor_1(M,O_S), plus its k-invariant ξ ∈ Ext^2(ω_G, n_G). These are to be shown to come from 'universal' data on B_π. In particular ξ is to come from a class ξ_Λ in Ext^2_Λ of π-modules, and for Λ = Z/n with M locally free over Λ, from H^2(π or S, End(M)). This prepares the study of deformations and obstructions of multiplicative-type groups, e.g. in characteristic p (crystals context).
errors: Minor: the 'universal covering' S' must be understood as a pro-object (profinite π = π_1) unless M is trivialised by a finite Galois covering. Grothendieck implicitly allows this ('profini').
Isotriviality criterion: SGA 3 X 5.16 requires S locally noetherian and normal. The page says 'fibres de type fini et S normal', which is fine up to noetherian hypotheses.
No mathematical errors in (1.4')–(1.8): flatness of O_S over a field and exactness/monoidality of f^* justify each step.

ideas.what: Co-Lie complex of a group of multiplicative type D(M) is M ⊗^L_Z O_S, computed via a resolution by tori and the transitivity triangle
ideas.modern_name: co-Lie complex ℓ_G of a multiplicative-type group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent et déformations II, 1972, ch. VII); Mazur–Roberts (1970) for the transitivity triangle
ideas.where_published: Illusie, Complexe cotangent II, ch. VII (based in part on Grothendieck's ideas)

ideas.what: Reduction mod a field Λ = F_p: ℓ^G ≃ (M⊗^L F_p)⊗_{F_p} O_S
ideas.modern_name: base change of derived tensor along flat map

ideas.what: Encoding an isotrivial M as pullback f^*M_0 along a morphism of topoi S → B_π, so that ℓ^G is pulled back from the classifying topos (tensored with O_S)
ideas.modern_name: descent of twisted-constant sheaves via classifying topos; ℓ^G as base change of a complex on B_π
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (classifying topos, SGA 4 IV); Illusie for co-Lie complexes
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 (classifying topos B_G) in general; not this specific application to my knowledge

missed.claim: The page (with the next one) sets up the idea that the k-invariant ξ ∈ Ext^2(ω_G, n_G) of the co-Lie complex of a multiplicative-type group is pulled back from a group-cohomology class of π (via B_π) and Λ = Z/n. This gives 'universal' obstruction classes in H^2(π, End(M_0)). The thread is not completed here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It gives a clean explanation of why deformation/obstruction invariants of isotrivial multiplicative groups factor through group cohomology of the monodromy group. However, this is a formal consequence of standard facts and is likely implicit in Illusie's treatment.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine computation of the co-Lie complex of multiplicative-type groups (published by Illusie), plus a formal factorisation through the classifying topos. Nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: The transcription duplicates a line ('noethérien[?]) et si S connexe, dans un sens dans le normal[?]) et si S connexe'). The image reads roughly: 'si M est isotrivial (p.ex. à fibres de t. fini et S [connexe, crossed out] normal) et si S connexe, dans ce cas dans la situation dite, avec S' le rev. universel de S....'
Line before (1.6) reads 'On a donc un morphisme de topos' ('Ou a donc' in handwriting); fine.
The label (1.7) belongs to M = f^*(M_0). The following equation M ⊗^L_Z Λ = f^*(M_0⊗^L_Z Λ) has a crossed-out label.
First line: 'Si p.ex. [crossed: ...] si Λ est un corps (p.ex. Λ = F_p), le L sur le dernier ⊗ est inutile'.
